claims.text: ADR 0027 header: not built at stage-4; Notifications still sends only email as at stage-3; the design and its review are in docs/design/notification-design-review.md.
The path from the API to the consumer stays as at stage-3 (outbox, a background job publishing to RabbitMQ); only what happens after the message reaches Notifications changes.
The consumer saves one row per channel the customer chose, in the same transaction as the inbox row; the Channel column of Notification already exists and is 'email' on every stage-3 row.
claims.source_hint: notification-design-review.md @ stage-4 lines 50-52; ADR 0027 lines 17-18, 35-36; DonHang.Notifications/Notification.cs line 15

claims.text: Each channel has its own sender with its own batch, retries and pace, a bulkhead between channels; each sender calls its provider through an interface of that channel, like IEmailSender.
Push waits for a phone build of the app, which Đơn Hàng does not have at stage-4 (ADR 0017).

Notifications owns notification preferences; the shop name is taken by shopId, an optional property order.* messages carry from rollout release 2; Notifications keeps a copy of the name (owner: Ordering's shops), its row to go into data-ownership.md when built.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0027 @ stage-4 Quyết định + Hệ quả ('dòng đó vào data-ownership.md khi xây'); docs/design/multi-shop-data-rollout.md lines 41-43

claims.text: SendDueAsync claims (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, locks held until CompleteAsync commits) up to BatchSize (10) due rows, awaits SendOneAsync for each in a foreach, then saves with CompleteAsync; it sees only IEmailSender, never MailKit, the library behind it.
Stage-3 NotificationSender retries after 2, 4, 8, 16 seconds; the fifth failure is final and the row becomes failed after about 30 seconds; a failed row is never retried automatically.
The review: 30 seconds is enough for Mailpit in the lab, not enough when an external email service is down a few minutes, because every email in that time becomes failed.

New design per ADR 0027: each channel retries for 24 hours (assumed), the gap growing to a maximum as Payments' RefundSender does when retrying refunds; after 24 hours the row becomes failed and is shown to operations to resend by hand.

Each sender stays under its provider's allowed rate; for email two copies of Notifications share 10 emails a second (assumed). ADR 0027: pacing so the backlog after an outage is sent without being refused.
ADR 0027 rejects one sending loop for every channel because a slow provider slows every other channel and all channels share one retry approach.
Estimate inputs reused: about 6.6 emails a second at the busiest hour, about 1.2 on a normal-day average, SMS about 0.7 a second at the peak (assumed).

MaxAttempts 20, doubling, no cap: gap after k failures is 2^k s; gaps before attempts 2-20 sum to 2^20-2 s, about 12 days, the last ones days long. A 4-hour outage (14,400 s) means about 13 failures, next gap at most 2^13 s, about 2.3 h.
claims.source_hint: Arithmetic from NotificationSender.cs @ stage-4 lines 16, 94 (delay = 2 s * 2^(attempts-1))

claims.text: Try it: with stage-3 retries an email first tried at second t fails finally at about t+30; for an outage 0-600 s at about 1.2 emails/s, about 1.2 x 570, roughly 700 emails end failed.
claims.source_hint: Arithmetic from NotificationSender.cs @ stage-4 lines 14-17 and the 1.2/s estimate

claims.text: Publishers keep sending the same order.* messages; the channel is chosen inside Notifications from the preferences it owns; the only message change relied on, shopId, comes from release 2 of the rollout.
An idempotent consumer's inbox row commits with its effect, so a repeated message adds no second set of rows.
Trade-off rows: one loop vs a sender per channel; give up after ~30 s vs retry 24 h (late email vs lost email, drivers 1-2); send at full speed vs pace to the allowed rate.
claims.source_hint: Derived from ADR 0027 lines 20-45 and notification-design-review.md lines 82-93

claims.text: If the SMS contract allows fewer than about 0.7 SMS a second, the SMS sender paces and SMS rows wait during the peak; emails are unaffected because their sender is separate; the drivers give no SMS delay number.
claims.source_hint: Follows from ADR 0027 lines 37-42 and the review's drivers lines 21-24
